h: Building a Badenoch day around the township
p: The Highland Folk Museum makes a superb centrepiece for a day in Badenoch, the stretch of Strathspey around Newtonmore and Kingussie. Start early at the museum, where the 1700s township of Baile Gean is a good first target as it sits at the far end of the site; if you head straight out there, you can work your way back through the later buildings towards the car park, with the 1930s croft and the old schoolhouse and shop on the way.

Keep an eye out for the period interpreters, who might be cooking, spinning or tending the animals, and don't be shy about asking questions. The schoolroom is a favourite with kids, especially if a stern teacher is in residence. There's a lot of walking between areas, so bring a snack and a drink, and pack a waterproof whatever the sky looks like when you set off.

For the afternoon, you're spoiled for choice. Newtonmore is home to the Clan Macpherson Museum, a nice small stop for anyone with Highland ancestry. Just south of Kingussie, the ruins of Ruthven Barracks sit dramatically on a mound above the River Spey, a powerful reminder of the Jacobite era and a superb spot for photographs. A little further up the A9, the Highland Wildlife Park near Kincraig is home to animals such as Scottish wildcats and polar bears, while Aviemore has the Strathspey Railway for a steam ride through the valley.
Mix and match those and you've got a cracking Cairngorms day, heavy on history and fresh air in equal measure.
